_: Shared handshake for the clock, loaded by every surface that faces the operator (the walker, the door shim, the desktop app), which must all give these answers. at = a UTC instant. et = the same instant on the America/Toronto wall clock (a label; EDT or EST says which of the two 01:xx hours of a fall-back night it is). dark = the ET wall-clock hour is in [2, 6), that is 02:00:00 through 05:59:59 ET (R-096 section 1). operator_day = the ET calendar date of the operator day the instant falls in; the day rolls at 02:00 ET on the wall clock (R-068 sections 1 and 5), so an ET hour below 2 still belongs to the previous date and midnight rolls nothing. Both answers come from the ET wall clock, never from a fixed UTC hour: 02:00 ET is 06:00Z in summer and 07:00Z in winter, so a surface that stores either one fails a vector here. operator_day equals the ET date of (the instant minus two hours) at every instant but one hour a year: in the repeated 01:xx hour of a fall-back night the wall clock still reads 01:xx, so the day has not rolled yet (2026-11-01 from 06:00:00Z to 06:59:59Z, marked by a note). Nothing in this file is a URL, a credential, a card id or a name.
